reason: The text contains multiple characters with clear agency. Most notably, Jael (wife of Heber the Kenite) is portrayed as a regular person who makes deliberate choices and takes decisive action—she invites Sisera into her tent, offers him hospitality, and then strategically kills him by driving a tent peg through his temple. She also demonstrates agency through her deception (instructing to say no one is present). Additionally, Deborah, while a prophet and judge, acts as an agent in commanding Barak and leading military strategy. Barak negotiates terms with Deborah before committing to the campaign. The Israelites collectively demonstrate agency by crying out to God. These are not passive figures being moved by divine will alone; they make decisions, give commands, negotiate, and execute plans.
